fixtures.basis: Arizona has no statewide code, so Phoenix's own code sets the counts. Phoenix leaves the 2024 IPC's Table 403.1 and Section 403.1.1 (half men, half women; fractions round up) unamended: neither appears in the city's IPC or IBC amendment packets (read in full for Chapter 4 and Chapter 29). Phoenix amends two rules beside the table: urinal substitution (424.2) and separate rooms (403.2 and IBC 2902.2). Under the Uniform Plumbing Code option the city replaces UPC Table 422.1 with IPC Table 403.1, so both plumbing codes give the same counts. The table rows themselves were read on UpCodes' copy of the Phoenix Plumbing Code 2024 (secondary).

amendment.text: (1) Urinals may replace no more than 50% of the men's required toilets in every occupancy; the model code's 67% for assembly and educational occupancies, and its 'in each bathroom or toilet room' wording, are struck. (2) Separate rooms for each sex are not required in business occupancies with 50 or fewer occupants (model: 25) or mercantile occupancies with 50 or fewer (model: 100); 15 or fewer in any occupancy, unchanged. (3) Under the UPC option, UPC Table 422.1 is replaced by IPC Table 403.1, with a footnote capping urinal substitution at 50%. Strikethroughs were read on page images of the city's PDF.
amendment.quote: 424.2 Substitution for water closets. Urinals shall not be substituted for more than 50 percent of the required water closets for males according to Table 403.1 in all occupancies. [...] 403.2 Separate facilities. [...] 3. Separate toilet facilities shall not be required in mercantile occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 50 or fewer. 4. Separate toilet facilities shall not be required in business occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 50 or fewer. [...] [UPC] Replace UPC Table 422.1 and footnotes with 2024 International Plumbing (IPC) Table 403.1 & footnotes. [...] h. Where urinals are provided they may be substituted for water closets, provided the number of water closets is not reduced to less than 50% of the minimum required by Table 422.1.

office.quote: Business: Buildings for the transaction of business, nonmedical professional services, other services involving merchandise, office buildings, banks, light industrial and similar uses: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50

restaurant.quote: Restaurants, banquet halls and food courts: 1 per 75 | 1 per 75

table_rows.split_rounding_quote: To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half. [...] Fractional numbers resulting from applying the fixture ratios of Table 403.1 shall be rounded up to the next whole number.
table_rows.all_gender_count_quote: Where multiple-user facilities are designed to serve all genders, the minimum fixture count shall be calculated 100 percent, based on total occupant load.

worked_examples.how: 25 women, 25 men. 1 per 25 for the first 50: 1 each. Urinals: not more than 50% of 1, so 0. At 50 or fewer occupants Phoenix does not require separate rooms for each sex in a business occupancy.
100 each. First 50: 2; remaining 50 at 1 per 50: 1; total 3 each. Urinals: 50% of 3 = 1.5, so 1.
200 each. First 50: 2; remaining 150 at 1 per 50: 3; total 5 each. Urinals: 50% of 5 = 2.5, so 2.
25 each. 25/75 rounds up to 1 each. Urinals: 0.
50 each. 50/75 rounds up to 1 each. Urinals: 0.
100 each. 100/75 = 1.33, rounds up to 2 each. Urinals: 50% of 2 = 1.
200 each. 200/75 = 2.67, rounds up to 3 each. Urinals: 50% of 3 = 1.5, so 1 (the model code's 67% would allow 2; Phoenix's 50% allows 1).
25 each. 25/50 rounds up to 1 each. Urinals: 0.

fixtures.worked_examples_note: Toilet counts equal the state pack's model figures; only the urinal allowance changes (restaurant at 400: 1, not 2). Urinals are optional, never required.

occupant_load.quote: Unconcentrated (tables and chairs) 15 net; Business areas 150 gross; Educational: Classroom area 20 net

permit.exempt_list_quote: [A] 105.2 Work exempt from permit. Exemptions from permit requirements of this code shall not be deemed to grant authorization for any work to be done in any manner in violation of the provisions of this code or any other laws or ordinances of the City of Phoenix. Permits shall not be required for the following: Building: [...] 7. Painting, papering, tiling excluding toilets areas, bathrooms and showers, carpeting, cabinets and counter top replacements in same location, and similar finish work. [...] 13. Fixtures, cases, racks, counters and partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches (1753 mm) in height and not an accessible surface. [...] 1. Minor repair or replacement in kind of non-structural components such as, glass or glazing materials, sash, doors, patching walls or ceilings and replacing pieces of siding, soffits or facia. Installation of locking or security hardware on egress doors, or changing the types of locking devices requires a permit.
permit.note: Item 13 names 'partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches in height' (Phoenix struck the model code's 'Nonfixed and movable'), but not toilet partitions or compartments, and doesn't say how the height is measured for a stall with taller pilasters. Item 7 excludes tiling in toilet areas from the finish-work exemption. Section 105.1 requires a permit to 'construct, enlarge, alter, repair' a building otherwise. The list doesn't decide the question for toilet partitions.
permit.required_quote: [A] 105.1 Required. Any owner or owner's authorized agent who intends to construct, enlarge, alter, repair, move, demolish or change the occupancy of a building or structure [...] shall first make application to the building official and obtain the required permit.
permit.office: City of Phoenix Planning and Development Department, Commercial

restrooms_city.rule: No separate city ordinance was found. Phoenix's adopted plumbing code (2024 IPC, these sections not amended away) sets both rules: single-user and family toilet rooms must be identified as available to all persons regardless of sex, and a shared room for all persons is allowed in place of separate rooms where each toilet is in a compartment with a door and each urinal is in its own partitioned area; the fixture count for such a room is worked on 100% of the occupants.
restrooms_city.quote: Single-user toilet facilities and bathing rooms, and family or assisted-use toilet facilities and bathing rooms shall be identified as being available for use by all persons regardless of their sex. [403.1.2, UpCodes copy] [...] 6. Separate toilet facilities shall not be required where rooms having both water closets and lavatory fixtures are designed for use by all persons regardless of sex and privacy is provided for water closets in accordance with Section 405.3.4 and for urinals in accordance with Section 405.3.5. [403.2 exception 6, city amendment PDF]
restrooms_city.note: Exception 6 is printed in the city's own amendment to 403.2 and IBC 2902.2. Sections 403.1.2, 405.3.4 and 405.3.5 were read on UpCodes (405.3.4 and 405.3.5 as a summary). How the Uniform Plumbing Code option treats shared all-gender rooms was not read. One web search found no Phoenix ordinance on restroom signs; the Phoenix City Code itself was not searched.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Phoenix job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material for the desert climate and see the rules that apply.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Phoenix offices, schools, resorts and distribution centers, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** Phoenix's building rules require solid plastic (HDPE) partitions to pass a fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Phoenix sets the number of toilets by how many people use the building, and caps how many of the men's toilets may be urinals. The table below shows what that means.
extra_rule_bullets: - **Phoenix access rules:** Phoenix names two accessibility standards for buildings: the federal one and a national standard, in its 2017 edition, that the city's building rules apply.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** under Phoenix's plumbing rules a one-person restroom must be marked as open to everyone. A shared all-gender room may take the place of separate men's and women's rooms if every toilet sits in its own compartment with a door and every urinal has its own partitioned area. A measure Arizona voters approved in November 2026 says that from January 1, 2027, a school or athletic association may not authorize anyone to use a restroom, locker room or shower room that is part of its athletics facilities and is not designated for that person's sex.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Phoenix requires a permit to alter a building unless the work is on its exempt list. The list covers painting, carpeting and similar finish work, and "fixtures, cases, racks, counters and partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches" high, but it doesn't say whether that includes toilet partitions. Ask Phoenix Planning and Development whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.stalls_intro: Arizona has no statewide building rules, so Phoenix's own rules decide. Phoenix counts toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women. Every toilet needs a stall. Urinals are optional: in Phoenix they may take the place of up to half of the men's toilets in any kind of building, so the table shows men's toilets as stalls.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for the whole building, and at least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible. An office or shop designed for 50 people or fewer, and any building designed for 15 or fewer, doesn't need separate men's and women's rooms. Confirm the count with Phoenix Planning and Development.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, Phoenix's building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20. Your architect or Phoenix Planning and Development sets the final number.
page.install_rule: Phoenix issues building permits only for work by state-licensed contractors, and the Arizona contractor's license number goes on the application. Arizona requires a state Registrar of Contractors license for commercial installation work of $1,000 or more. Confirm what your project needs with Phoenix Planning and Development. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: A contractor on a commercial job of $1,000 or more in Arizona needs a state Registrar of Contractors license.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** Arizona has no wage law for public jobs, and state law bars cities, counties and school districts from requiring prevailing wages in their contracts. On federally funded work the federal rate applies: $33.19 an hour plus $19.20 in benefits for a carpenter on building work in Maricopa County.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 9.1% in Phoenix: 5.6% state, 0.7% Maricopa County and 2.8% city.
page.buyers_extra: - **Resorts, golf clubs and sports venues:** finishes that match the property in guest restrooms, HDPE or phenolic in pool and locker room restrooms that are hosed down.

- Toilet counts in Phoenix: Phoenix amendments to the [2024 International Plumbing Code](https://www.phoenix.gov/content/dam/phoenix/pddsite/documents/codes-ordinances/amendmentcodes/2024-ipc.pdf), Sections 403.2 and 424.2, to the [2024 Uniform Plumbing Code](https://www.phoenix.gov/content/dam/phoenix/pddsite/documents/codes-ordinances/amendmentcodes/2024-upc.pdf), Table 422.1, and to the [2024 International Building Code](https://www.phoenix.gov/content/dam/phoenix/pddsite/documents/codes-ordinances/amendmentcodes/2024-ibc.pdf), Section 2902.2. The unamended Table 403.1 and Sections 403.1.1 and 403.1.2 were read on a [secondary copy of the Phoenix Plumbing Code 2024](https://up.codes/viewer/phoenix/ipc-2024/chapter/4/fixtures-faucets-and-fixture-fittings). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Floor area per person and the fire test for solid plastic: 2024 International Building Code as adopted by Phoenix, Table 1004.5 and Sections 803.9 and 803.1.1 (NFPA 286), not amended by the city, read on a secondary copy of the Phoenix Building Code 2024 ([Chapter 10](https://up.codes/viewer/phoenix/ibc-2024/chapter/10/means-of-egress), [Chapter 8](https://up.codes/viewer/phoenix/ibc-2024/chapter/8/interior-finishes)). Checked 2026-11-24.

Checked 2026-11-24.

- Maricopa County carpenter rate on federally funded building work: [federal wage determination AZ20260039, modification 1, May 18, 2026](https://sam.gov/wage-determination/AZ20260039/1). Checked 2026-11-24.
page.official_names: - The rules by their official names: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design (adopted by A.A.C. R10-3-404 under the Arizonans with Disabilities Act, A.R.S. 41-1492 et seq.); ICC A117.1-2017 as scoped in the amended 2024 International Building Code; 2024 Phoenix Building Construction Code (Ordinance G-7397, in force since August 1, 2025): 2024 International Building Code with Phoenix amendments, including its Administrative Provisions (Chapter 1, Section 105.2 for work exempt from permits), and the 2024 International Plumbing Code or 2024 Uniform Plumbing Code, each with Phoenix amendments; NFPA 286 for HDPE (International Building Code Section 803.9).
notes: To confirm by phone before launch: whether replacing or adding toilet partitions needs a Phoenix permit, and whether exempt item 13 ('partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches in height') covers them (Planning and Development, Commercial, 602-534-6502, pdd.commercial.building@phoenix.gov).

The unamended parts of Phoenix's code (toilet table, floor area per person, the HDPE fire-test section, single-user restroom signs) were read on UpCodes, not on ICC's site: check once in a browser at codes.iccsafe.org/codes/united-states/arizona/phoenix.
The fire-test section says 'used as an interior finish' and doesn't name toilet partitions (same wording as other cities' pages).
Phoenix accepts the Uniform Plumbing Code as an alternative to the International Plumbing Code; its toilet table is replaced by the same table, but how it treats shared all-gender rooms was not read.

Phoenix's own prevailing wage ordinance (2024) was ruled unlawful by the Arizona Court of Appeals on February 27, 2026 according to news reports; not read on an official page, so not in the page text.
Sales tax: Phoenix's city rate falls to 2.0% on the part of a single item's price over $14,338; left off the page, add it if single items of that size are ever quoted.
What ICC A117.1-2017 changes for stalls compared with the federal standard was not read; the access bullet only says both apply.

The Arizona state pack's source bullets on the national model code (Kansas and New Hampshire copies, 2018 edition) print in this page's Sources list although Phoenix's own 2024 code is cited above them: consider dropping them for cities with their own pack entries.
